examples.ko: 봄에 시장에서 취나물을 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: In spring I bought a bag of chwinamul at the market.
Chwinamul is delicious when you blanch it and toss it with sesame oil.

examples.ko: 어머니가 취나물 반찬을 자주 해 주세요.
examples.en: My mother often makes chwinamul side dishes for me.
I made rice with chwinamul picked in the mountains.
This restaurant is famous for its chwinamul bibimbap.

examples.ko: 취나물 향이 너무 좋아서 밥을 두 그릇 먹었어요.
examples.en: The chwinamul smelled so good that I ate two bowls of rice.

explain: 봄나물로 많이 먹고 나물 반찬이나 비빔밥, 나물밥에 들어가요. 보통 '취나물을 데치다/무치다/볶다'처럼 요리 동사와 함께 써요. 식당 메뉴에서도 자주 볼 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is eaten a lot as a spring wild vegetable, in side dishes, bibimbap and namul rice. It usually goes with cooking verbs like '취나물을 데치다/무치다/볶다' (blanch/toss/stir-fry). You will also see it often on restaurant menus.

examples.en: The job shortage among young people is really serious these days.

examples.ko: 취직난 때문에 졸업을 미루는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students put off graduating because of the job shortage.
When the economy gets worse, the job shortage gets worse too.
The news keeps talking about the job shortage.

examples.ko: 취직난을 해결하려면 일자리가 더 늘어야 해요.
examples.en: To solve the job shortage, there need to be more jobs.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 오래전부터 취직난에 시달리고 있어요.
examples.en: This country has suffered from a job shortage for a long time.

explain: '취업난'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 보통 '취직난이 심하다/심각하다', '취직난에 시달리다'처럼 말해요. 반대로 일할 사람을 구하기 어려운 상황은 '구인난'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '취업난' is used with almost the same meaning. People usually say '취직난이 심하다/심각하다' or '취직난에 시달리다'. The opposite situation, where employers cannot find workers, is called '구인난'.

examples.en: I'm looking for a job before I graduate.

examples.ko: 좋은 취직자리가 나서 친구가 아주 기뻐해요.
examples.en: A good job opening came up, and my friend is very happy.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 제 취직자리를 하나 소개해 줬어요.
examples.en: My uncle introduced me to a job opening.
It isn't easy to find a job these days.
There aren't many job openings in this city.
I asked my senior about job openings.

explain: '일자리'와 비슷하지만 '취직자리'는 직장에 들어가서 일하게 될 자리라는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '취직자리를 구하다/알아보다/소개하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '일자리', but '취직자리' carries the feel of a position you get by entering a company. It usually appears as '취직자리를 구하다/알아보다/소개하다' (look for/check/recommend).

examples.en: I stacked the cake in layers and made it look pretty.
The books are placed on the shelves tier by tier.
Rice paddies spread out in terraces on the mountain slope.

examples.ko: 옷을 층층이 겹쳐 입으면 덜 추워요.
examples.en: If you wear clothes in layers, you feel less cold.
I packed the side dishes in the lunch box in layers.

examples.ko: 눈이 층층이 쌓여서 길이 안 보여요.
examples.en: The snow has piled up layer upon layer, so I can't see the road.

explain: '겹겹이'와 비슷하지만 '층층이'는 층이 나뉘어 쌓인 모양에 어울려요. '층층이 쌓다/쌓이다/놓다'처럼 자주 써요. 칸으로 나뉜 모양은 '칸칸이'를 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '겹겹이', but '층층이' fits things stacked in distinct tiers. It is common in '층층이 쌓다/쌓이다/놓다'. For things divided into compartments, use '칸칸이'.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 말로 치고받다가 결국 화해했어요.
examples.en: The two traded harsh words, but in the end they made up.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 형이랑 자주 치고받고 싸웠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I often fought back and forth with my older brother.
The kids are playing around, roughhousing with each other.

examples.ko: 회의에서 두 팀이 서로 치고받는 분위기였어요.
examples.en: At the meeting, the two teams were arguing fiercely with each other.
On the debate show, the candidates traded sharp words.
The siblings were going at each other from the morning, so Mom stopped them.

explain: 서로 주고받는 상황에 써요. 몸으로 싸울 때뿐 아니라 '말로 치고받다'처럼 말다툼이 심할 때도 써요. 보통 '치고받고 싸우다'라는 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when both sides give and take. It covers physical scuffles and also heated arguments, as in '말로 치고받다'. It often appears in the form '치고받고 싸우다'.

examples.en: In summer I often wear cool pantskirts.
A pantskirt looks like a skirt, but it's comfortable.
My daughter went to school wearing a pantskirt.
Where did you buy this pantskirt?
A pantskirt is comfortable when you ride a bike.
My friend came wearing a pantskirt and sneakers.

explain: 치마처럼 넓지만 바지처럼 다리가 나뉜 옷이라 움직이기 편해요. 입을 때는 '입다'를 써요. 비슷하게 바지 종류를 말하는 '반바지', '칠부바지'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is wide like a skirt but split like trousers, so it is easy to move in. The verb for wearing it is '입다'. It is useful to learn it with other pants words such as '반바지' and '칠부바지'.

examples.en: On New Year's Day, my grandmother wears a lovely chima jeogori.
The children bowed wearing chima jeogori.
The colors of the chima jeogori are really bright.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 치마저고리를 입어 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can try on a chima jeogori at the museum.
My mother came to the wedding dressed in chima jeogori.
My mother made this chima jeogori herself.

explain: 여성 한복의 치마와 저고리를 함께 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '한복'이라고도 해요. 남성 한복은 '바지저고리'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It names the skirt and jacket of a woman's hanbok together. In daily talk people often just say '한복'. The men's version is called '바지저고리'.

en: hem of a skirt; trailing part of a skirt

examples.en: The hem of her skirt fluttered slightly in the wind.
The child held tightly onto her mother's skirt.
I stepped on my skirt on the stairs and almost fell.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 치맛자락이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: On the rainy day, the bottom of my skirt got soaked.
I held my skirt and walked carefully.

examples.ko: 문에 치맛자락이 끼어서 움직일 수 없었어요.
examples.en: My skirt got caught in the door, so I couldn't move.

explain: 치마의 아래쪽으로 늘어진 부분을 말해요. 옷감을 접어 꿰맨 끝 가장자리는 '치맛단'이라고 해서 조금 달라요. '치맛자락을 잡다/밟다/끌다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the lower part of a skirt that hangs down. The folded and stitched edge is called '치맛단', which is a bit different. It goes with verbs like '치맛자락을 잡다/밟다/끌다'.

examples.en: I got hemorrhoids from sitting and working for a long time.
I had hemorrhoid surgery and rested for a week.
My hemorrhoids got worse, so I went to the hospital.
If you have constipation, you easily get hemorrhoids.

examples.ko: 아버지가 치질 때문에 오래 앉아 있기 힘들어하세요.
examples.en: My father has a hard time sitting for long because of hemorrhoids.

examples.ko: 치질은 부끄러워하지 말고 빨리 치료받아야 해요.
examples.en: Don't be embarrassed about hemorrhoids; get treated quickly.

explain: '양치질'의 '치질' 부분과 모양이 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉽지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 이를 닦는 건 '양치질', 이건 항문의 병이에요. '치질에 걸리다/치질이 생기다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It looks like the last part of '양치질', so it is easy to mix up, but they are unrelated. Brushing teeth is '양치질', while this is a condition of the anus. You say '치질에 걸리다' or '치질이 생기다'.

examples.ko: 선생님이 그 학생을 반 대표라며 치켜세웠어요.
examples.en: The teacher praised that student highly as the class representative.
Please don't praise me too much, I'm embarrassed.

examples.ko: 화가 난 그는 눈썹을 치켜세우고 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: He was angry and raised his eyebrows as he looked at me.

examples.ko: 친구들이 저를 치켜세워 줘서 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: My friends built me up, and I felt good.
The boss flattered the staff while giving them work.

examples.ko: 아무리 치켜세워도 그 사람은 돕지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: No matter how much you flatter him, he won't help.

explain: 눈썹이나 고개처럼 위로 올릴 때도 쓰고, 사람을 실제보다 높게 칭찬해 줄 때도 써요. 두 번째 뜻은 '추켜세우다'와 같게 쓰이고, 아부하는 듯한 느낌이 들 수 있어요. 진심 어린 칭찬에는 '칭찬하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means to lift something up, like eyebrows or a chin, and also to praise someone more highly than they deserve. The second meaning is the same as '추켜세우다' and can sound like flattery. For sincere praise, '칭찬하다' is more natural.

en: paternal family; relatives on one's father's side

examples.en: On holidays we visit both my father's side and my mother's side.

examples.ko: 저는 친가 쪽 친척이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't have many relatives on my father's side.
My father's family is from Busan and my mother's is from Gwangju.
During vacation I helped my grandmother at my father's family home.
I often meet my cousins on my father's side.

examples.ko: 제 친가 식구들은 모두 서울에 살아요.
examples.en: All my father's relatives live in Seoul.

explain: 아버지 쪽 집안을 말하고, 어머니 쪽은 '외가'라고 해요. '친가 쪽 친척'처럼 '쪽'과 함께 자주 써요. 결혼한 여자의 부모님 집을 뜻하는 '친정'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It means your father's side of the family; your mother's side is '외가'. It is often used with '쪽', as in '친가 쪽 친척'. It is different from '친정', which is a married woman's parents' home.

examples.en: There is an alumni get-together this weekend.
The company is collecting dues for the social club.
I met my seniors after a long time at the get-together.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 친목회는 한 달에 한 번 모여요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood social club meets once a month.
I'm busy these days because I took on the role of treasurer of the social club.

examples.ko: 그 모임은 이름은 친목회지만 실제로는 사업 이야기만 해요.
examples.en: That group is called a social club, but they only talk business.

explain: 서로 친해지려고 모이는 모임이에요. 같은 취미로 모이는 '동호회', 같은 학교 출신이 모이는 '동창회'와 달리 특별한 조건 없이 가볍게 모여요. '친목회를 하다/열다/가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a group that meets just to get closer to each other. Unlike a '동호회' (hobby club) or '동창회' (alumni association), it often has no special condition. You say '친목회를 하다/열다/가다'.

examples.en: She raised someone else's child like her own.
Whether biological or adopted, they are all precious family.
My grandmother cherishes her daughter-in-law like her own child.
He isn't my own child, but we've grown very close.
They say there are secrets that are hard to tell even your own child.
Thank you for treating me as well as your own child.

explain: 직접 낳은 자식을 말해요. 남을 아주 가깝게 대할 때 '친자식처럼'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 새 배우자의 자식은 '의붓자식'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a child you gave birth to yourself. It is also often used figuratively as '친자식처럼' (like one's own child) for treating others very warmly. A new spouse's child is called '의붓자식'.

examples.en: Even after marriage, I call my father often.
My father sent me kimchi.
My father farms in the countryside.
It's my father's birthday, so I'm going down this weekend.
I'm tall because I take after my father.
I left my child with my father and went to work.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 아버지를 말할 때 써요. 남편의 아버지는 '시아버지', 남자가 아내의 아버지를 말할 때는 '장인어른'이라고 해요. 결혼 전의 딸이 말할 때는 그냥 '아버지'를 써요.
explain_en: A married woman uses this for her own father. Her husband's father is '시아버지', and a man calls his wife's father '장인어른'. An unmarried daughter would simply say '아버지'.

en: the former home of a married woman

examples.en: I went to my parents' home for the holiday and rested.
My parents' home is close, so I stop by often.
The married daughter came to visit her parents' home.
There is a persimmon tree in the yard of my parents' home.
They packed lots of side dishes for me at my parents' home.
The new bride missed her parents' home and cried in secret.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 자기 부모님이 사는 집을 말해요. 짧게 '친정'이라고도 하고, 보통 '친정에 가다'처럼 써요. 남편 부모님 집은 '시댁'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the home of a married woman's own parents. It is often shortened to '친정', as in '친정에 가다'. Her husband's parents' home is '시댁'.

examples.en: In spring, three-quarter pants go well with sneakers.
Three-quarter pants show your ankles, so they feel cool.
I'm short, so three-quarter pants are as long as full pants on me.
I went to the mall to buy a pair of three-quarter pants.

examples.ko: 이 칠부바지는 회사에 입고 가기 좋아요.
examples.en: These three-quarter pants are good to wear to work.
It got hot, so I changed into three-quarter pants.

explain: 무릎과 발목 사이, 종아리쯤까지 오는 바지예요. 무릎 위까지 오는 '반바지'와 발목까지 닿는 '긴바지'의 중간이라 봄과 가을에 입기 편해요. 단정해 보여서 회사에도 입고 가요. '칠부바지를 입다/사다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: These pants reach about the calf, between the knee and the ankle. They sit between '반바지' (shorts) and '긴바지' (long pants), so they are handy in spring and autumn. They look neat enough to wear to work. You say '칠부바지를 입다/사다'.

examples.en: I booked a sleeper car on the train and traveled comfortably.
I slept well in the sleeper and woke up to find we had arrived.
The sleeping compartment is more expensive than a regular seat.

examples.ko: 아이들이 처음 타 보는 침대칸을 신기해해요.
examples.en: The kids find the sleeper car they are riding for the first time fascinating.

examples.ko: 밤 기차는 침대칸 표가 금방 매진돼요.
examples.en: On night trains, the sleeper tickets sell out quickly.
I could see mountains outside the window of the sleeper.

explain: 기차나 배에서 누워 잘 수 있게 만든 칸이에요. 앉아서 가는 칸은 '좌석칸'이나 '일반석'이라고 해요. '침대칸을 타다/예약하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a compartment on a train or ship where you can lie down and sleep. The seated section is called '좌석칸' or '일반석'. You say '침대칸을 타다/예약하다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 위기에서도 침착성을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player didn't lose his composure even in a crisis.

examples.ko: 불이 났을 때는 침착성이 있는 사람이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: When there's a fire, a person with composure is helpful.
My younger sibling lacks composure and often makes mistakes.
Appearing composed is important in an interview.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 침착성을 가르치는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Teaching children to be composed is not easy.
Composure can be built up little by little with practice.

explain: 그 사람의 성격이나 태도를 말할 때 써요. 지금 이 순간의 모습은 '침착해요', '침착하게'가 더 자연스러워요. '침착성이 있다/없다/부족하다', '침착성을 잃다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it for a person's character or general attitude. For how someone is right now, '침착해요' or '침착하게' is more natural. It appears as '침착성이 있다/없다/부족하다' and '침착성을 잃다'.

examples.en: I always brush my teeth after meals.

examples.ko: 칫솔질을 너무 세게 하면 잇몸이 상해요.
examples.en: If you brush too hard, your gums get hurt.

examples.ko: 아이에게 올바른 칫솔질 방법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: I showed my child the right way to brush teeth.

examples.ko: 칫솔질은 하루에 세 번 하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to brush your teeth three times a day.
I was sleepy and fell asleep without even brushing my teeth.
After brushing, I rinse my mouth well.

explain: 같은 상황에서 '양치질'이나 '양치'도 많이 써요. '칫솔질'은 칫솔로 닦는 동작을 구체적으로 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '칫솔질을 하다', '올바른 칫솔질'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In the same situation, '양치질' or '양치' is also widely used. '칫솔질' fits well when you talk specifically about the act of brushing with a toothbrush. It appears in '칫솔질을 하다' and '올바른 칫솔질'.

examples.en: The chameleon is famous as an animal that changes color.
At the zoo, a chameleon was sitting on a branch.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 카멜레온처럼 상황에 따라 변해요.
examples.en: That person changes like a chameleon depending on the situation.
My friend keeps a chameleon as a pet.
A chameleon's eyes move separately on each side.
He has a chameleon-like personality, so he's hard to trust.

explain: 동물 이름이지만 사람에게 쓰면 비유예요. 상황마다 태도를 바꾸는 사람을 '카멜레온 같다'고 말하는데, 칭찬보다는 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 카멜레온 같아서 누구 앞에서든 말이 달라져요.
phrases.en: to be like a chameleon (changing one's attitude to suit the situation)
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황이나 사람에 따라 태도와 말을 바꾸는 사람을 가리켜요. 약간 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who changes attitude and words depending on the situation or person. Slightly negative.

explain_en: It is an animal name, but used for a person it is a metaphor. People say '카멜레온 같다' about someone who changes attitude with each situation, which sounds slightly sarcastic rather than complimentary.

examples.en: I received career counseling at school.

examples.ko: 스트레스가 심해서 카운슬링을 받아 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I was so stressed that I decided to try counseling.
Thanks to the counseling, I feel much more at ease.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 직원 카운슬링 시간을 운영해요.
examples.en: Our company runs counseling hours for employees.

examples.ko: 카운슬링을 하는 선생님이 친절하게 들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher who does counseling listened to me kindly.

examples.ko: 이 센터에서 무료 카운슬링을 해 줘요.
examples.en: This center offers free counseling.

explain: '상담'으로 바꿔 말해도 돼요. 카운슬링은 마음 고민이나 진로처럼 이야기를 들어 주고 조언하는 상담에 잘 어울려요. '카운슬링을 받다/하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: You can often replace it with '상담'. '카운슬링' suits sessions where someone listens and advises on worries or career choices. It goes with '카운슬링을 받다/하다'.

examples.en: Khaki pants go well with almost anything.
It's autumn, so I bought a khaki jacket.
Which is better, khaki or black?
Decorating the room in khaki makes it look calm.

examples.ko: 그 가방은 카키색이라서 때가 덜 타요.
examples.en: That bag is khaki, so it doesn't show dirt as much.
I wore a white T-shirt with a khaki coat.

explain: 옷 색을 말할 때 많이 써요. 색 이름 뒤의 '색'을 빼고 '카키 바지'처럼도 말해요. 같은 외래어 색 이름으로 '베이지색', '네이비색' 등이 있어요.
explain_en: It is commonly used for clothing colors. You can drop '색' and say '카키 바지'. Other loanword colors are '베이지색' and '네이비색'.

examples.en: I ate lunch at the school cafeteria.

examples.ko: 카페테리아에서는 먼저 쟁반을 들고 줄을 서요.
examples.en: At a cafeteria, you first pick up a tray and line up.
The company cafeteria menu is decent today.
I had coffee with a friend at the cafeteria.
There is a cafeteria in the basement of this building.
The cafeteria was crowded, so I couldn't find a seat.

explain: '카페'와 달리 음식을 직접 골라 담아 먹는 식당이에요. 학교는 '학생식당', 회사는 '구내식당'이라고도 말해요. 외국 영화나 학교 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Unlike a '카페', it is a place where you pick and carry your own food. At schools people also say '학생식당', and at companies '구내식당'. You often hear it in stories about foreign schools.

en: room by room; cell by cell

examples.en: I divided the drawer into compartments and organized my socks.

examples.ko: 기차 안을 칸칸이 살펴봤지만 친구가 없었어요.
examples.en: I searched the train car by car, but my friend wasn't there.

examples.ko: 약통에 요일별로 약이 칸칸이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The pill box has medicine in each compartment by day of the week.
I filled the box compartment by compartment and wrapped the gift.

examples.ko: 공책에 한 글자씩 칸칸이 써 넣었어요.
examples.en: I wrote one letter per box in the notebook.

examples.ko: 아파트 창문마다 불빛이 칸칸이 켜져 있어요.
examples.en: Lights are on in each window of the apartment, box after box.

explain: 칸 하나하나마다라는 느낌이라 '칸마다'로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요. '층층이'는 위아래로 쌓인 층에, '칸칸이'는 나뉜 칸에 써요. '칸칸이 나누다/채우다/적다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of 'in each compartment', so you can swap it with '칸마다'. '층층이' is for stacked tiers, while '칸칸이' is for divided boxes or compartments. It is common in '칸칸이 나누다/채우다/적다'.

examples.en: I carefully cut out the potato sprouts with the tip of the knife.
The tip of this knife is sharp, so be careful.

examples.ko: 요리사는 칼끝을 살짝 세워 칼집을 냈어요.
examples.en: The chef tilted the tip of the knife slightly and scored the food.
Be careful that your hand doesn't touch the knife tip.

examples.ko: 칼끝을 아래로 향하게 두고 건네지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't hand it over with the tip pointing down.
I cut the packing tape gently with the knife tip.

explain: 칼의 뾰족한 끝부분이에요. 칼의 다른 부분은 날 쪽이 '칼날', 뒤쪽이 '칼등', 손잡이가 '칼자루'예요. '붓끝', '펜 끝'처럼 '-끝'이 붙는 말과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the pointed end of a knife. Other parts are '칼날' (blade edge), '칼등' (back of the blade) and '칼자루' (handle). It helps to learn it alongside words ending in '-끝', such as '붓끝' (brush tip).

examples.en: My ears were numb in the icy wind of the winter morning.
An icy wind is blowing, so I don't want to go out.
When I went out to the Han River, the wind was really biting.
I waited for the bus in the biting wind.

examples.ko: 오늘은 칼바람 때문에 체감온도가 더 낮아요.
examples.en: Today the felt temperature is lower because of the icy wind.

examples.ko: 이럴 땐 목도리로 칼바람을 막아야 해요.
examples.en: At times like this you have to block the icy wind with a scarf.

explain: '찬바람'보다 훨씬 날카롭게 살을 에는 듯한 겨울바람에 써요. 보통 '칼바람이 불다/몰아치다'라고 해요. 글에서는 '삭풍'이라는 말도 있지만 대화에서는 '칼바람'이 더 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used for a winter wind that feels sharper than a plain '찬바람' and cuts into the skin. You usually say '칼바람이 불다/몰아치다'. There is also the literary word '삭풍', but '칼바람' is closer to everyday speech.

examples.ko: 칼자루를 잡을 때는 손이 미끄럽지 않아야 해요.
examples.en: Your hand shouldn't be slippery when you hold the knife handle.

examples.ko: 이 칼은 칼자루가 나무로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This knife has a wooden handle.
The handle was loose, so I bought a new knife.

examples.ko: 요리할 때 칼자루를 꽉 쥐고 썰어요.
examples.en: When cooking, I grip the handle firmly and chop.

examples.ko: 할아버지 칼은 칼자루에 손때가 묻어 있어요.
examples.en: Grandfather's knife has years of hand wear on its handle.
Please hand it over with the handle side forward.

explain: 칼의 손잡이 부분이에요. 칼날 쪽과 짝으로 알아 두세요. '칼자루를 쥐다'는 실제 칼이 아니라 결정할 힘을 가졌다는 비유로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이번 협상은 우리가 칼자루를 쥐고 있어요.
phrases.en: to hold the power to decide; have the upper hand
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정권이나 주도권이 내게 있다는 뜻이에요. '칼자루를 잡다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you hold the decision-making power or the initiative. Also said as '칼자루를 잡다'.

explain_en: It is the handle part of a knife, the counterpart of the blade. '칼자루를 쥐다' is also widely used figuratively, not about a real knife but about holding the power to decide.

examples.en: That chef is very quick with the knife.

examples.ko: 양파를 썰 때는 칼질을 천천히 해야 해요.
examples.en: When slicing onions, you have to cut slowly.

examples.ko: 도마에서 나는 칼질 소리가 규칙적으로 들려요.
examples.en: I hear the rhythmic sound of chopping on the cutting board.
My knife work is clumsy, so the carrots are uneven.
It looks cool to watch him cut on the cutting board.

examples.ko: 레스토랑에서 스테이크 칼질을 처음 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I cut a steak with a knife at a restaurant for the first time.

explain: 재료를 칼로 써는 동작이나 그 솜씨를 말해요. 솜씨를 말할 때는 '칼질이 빠르다/서툴다/능숙하다'처럼 써요. 칼로 써는 서양식 식사를 가볍게 '칼질'이라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the act or skill of cutting food with a knife. For skill you say '칼질이 빠르다/서툴다/능숙하다'. People also casually call a knife-and-fork Western-style meal '칼질'.

examples.en: I scored the sausage and grilled it.

examples.ko: 생선에 칼집을 넣으면 양념이 잘 배요.
examples.en: If you score the fish, the seasoning soaks in well.
Squid with scored cuts curls up like a flower.

examples.ko: 칼집이 깊으면 고기가 부서질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the cuts are deep, the meat can fall apart.
The sauce seeps right into the cuts.

examples.ko: 감자 겉에 칼집을 몇 군데 넣었어요.
examples.en: I made a few cuts on the surface of the potato.

explain: 요리에서는 재료 겉에 얕게 낸 칼자국을 말해요. '칼집을 내다/넣다'라고 말해요. 같은 모양의 '칼집'은 칼을 꽂아 두는 물건이라는 뜻도 있어서 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: In cooking it means shallow cuts made on the surface of food, as in '칼집을 내다/넣다'. The same-looking word '칼집' also means a sheath for holding a knife, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: I sang songs with my friends in front of the campfire.
We had a campfire on the last day of the retreat.
The light of the campfire was really warm.
The campfire was canceled because of rain.
We sat around the campfire and roasted marshmallows.
The kids are looking forward to the campfire the most.

explain: 캠핑이나 수련회에서 모여 앉아 즐기는 불 행사를 말해요. 불 자체는 '모닥불'이라고 해요. '캠프파이어를 하다'처럼 행사 느낌으로 쓰고, '모닥불을 피우다'처럼 불을 지핀다는 느낌으로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the event of gathering around a fire at a camp or retreat. The fire itself is '모닥불'. You say '캠프파이어를 하다' for the event and '모닥불을 피우다' for lighting the fire.

examples.ko: 방 안이 너무 컴컴해서 아무것도 안 보여요.
examples.en: The room is so dark that I can't see anything.
When evening came, the alley turned dark.
It's scary to walk alone on a dark road.

examples.ko: 정전이 돼서 집 안이 온통 컴컴해요.
examples.en: There's a power outage, so the whole house is pitch-dark.
When I turned off the light, the room turned dark.

examples.ko: 터널 안은 컴컴해도 전조등을 켜면 괜찮아요.
examples.en: The tunnel is dark, but it's fine if you turn on the headlights.

explain: '캄캄하다'와 모음만 달라서 어감이 더 크고 묵직해요. '어둡다'보다 훨씬 깜깜한 느낌이고, '어두컴컴하다'처럼 합쳐서도 써요. 변화는 '컴컴해지다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It differs from '캄캄하다' only in vowels and sounds bigger and heavier. It feels much darker than '어둡다' and also appears in '어두컴컴하다'. Change is often said as '컴컴해지다'.

en: area under the nose; upper lip area

examples.en: Beads of sweat formed under my nose.

examples.ko: 아이가 코밑에 우유 자국이 묻어 있어요.
examples.en: The child has a milk mark under the nose.
The skin under my nose was sore, so I put on ointment.
I wiped under my nose with a tissue.
There's a man with a mustache.
My younger sibling pulled the blanket up to the nose and slept.

explain: 코와 윗입술 사이의 몸 부위예요. 가까운 거리나 시간을 비유로 말할 때는 '코밑'이 아니라 '코앞'을 써요(시험이 코앞이에요). '코밑 수염'은 콧수염을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is the body area between the nose and upper lip. For something very close in distance or time, use '코앞' rather than '코밑' (e.g., the exam is right around the corner). '코밑 수염' refers to a mustache.

examples.ko: 그는 제 말을 듣고 코웃음을 쳤어요.
examples.en: He scoffed when he heard what I said.

examples.ko: 친구가 코웃음 치면서 못 믿겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: My friend sneered and said he couldn't believe it.
Everyone just scoffed, saying it was impossible, but I did it.
It was such an absurd proposal that it made me scoff.
Even to such praise, she responded with a scoff.

examples.ko: 선배가 제 계획을 코웃음 한 번으로 넘겼어요.
examples.en: My senior dismissed my plan with a single scoff.

explain: 상대를 얕보거나 믿지 않을 때 코로 '흥' 하고 내는 웃음이에요. 보통 '코웃음을 치다'로 써요. 소리 내어 웃는 '비웃다'보다 짧고 차갑게 무시하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a short 'hmph' laugh through the nose when you look down on or doubt someone. It is usually said as '코웃음을 치다'. Compared with '비웃다', it feels shorter and more coldly dismissive.

examples.en: My nose hair was sticking out, so I cut it with scissors.
When you pull out nose hair, your eyes water.
I received a nose hair trimmer as a gift.

examples.ko: 먼지를 걸러 주는 코털도 하는 일이 있어요.
examples.en: Nose hair has a job too, filtering out dust.
Before the interview, I even neatly trimmed my nose hair.
My husband is worried about his nose hair.

explain: '코털을 뽑다/자르다/다듬다'처럼 써요. 일상에서 흔한 말이지만 조금 민망한 주제라서 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 꺼내지 않아요. 편한 사이에서 외모 이야기를 할 때 주로 나와요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs such as '코털을 뽑다/자르다/다듬다'. It is a common word, but the topic is a little embarrassing, so people avoid it in formal settings. It mostly comes up between close people talking about appearance.

examples.en: I poked holes with a needle.
The bird pecks at its food.
My head throbs with sharp pains.

examples.ko: 반죽에 포크로 콕콕 구멍을 내 주세요.
examples.en: Please poke holes in the dough with a fork.
Try tapping the screen with your finger.

examples.ko: 아이가 제 어깨를 콕콕 찔러서 깼어요.
examples.en: The child poked my shoulder, and I woke up.

explain: 작고 뾰족한 것으로 가볍게 여러 번 찌르거나 쪼는 모양이에요. '쿡쿡'이 더 깊고 세게 찌르는 느낌이라면 '콕콕'은 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요. '콕콕 쑤시다'처럼 아픔에도 써요.
explain_en: It describes poking or pecking lightly several times with something small and pointed. Compared with '쿡쿡', which feels deeper and stronger, '콕콕' feels smaller and lighter. It is also used for pain, as in '콕콕 쑤시다'.
